# Pipeline

Four stages, one Prisma table each, chained only by the shape of the data. A stage finds
its work by querying for rows whose *downstream* relation is still `null`, so every stage
is independently re-runnable and safe to run twice.

| Stage | Endpoint | Finds work by | Writes |
|-------|----------|---------------|--------|
| Sync | `POST /email-sync/:id/run` | `SyncState.lastSyncedUid` watermark | `RawEmail` |
| Parse | `POST /email-parser/run` | `rawEmail.parsed: null` | `ParsedEmail` |
| Normalize | `POST /normalization/run` | `parsedEmail.normalized: null` | `NormalizedEmail` |
| Classify | `POST /classification/run` | `normalizedEmail.classification: null` | `EmailClassification` |

## Stage 1 — Sync

[`syncAccount()`](mex://method:efd8143865e919dd229b149ab5736020) is the production ingestion
path. It rejects the account up front if it is missing, `isActive: false`, or
`needsReauth: true`; resolves credentials through `EmailAccountsService.getImapCredentials`;
upserts a `SyncState` row per `(accountId, mailbox)`; flips it to `SYNCING`; and fetches the
UID range `1:*` on a first run or `${lastSyncedUid + 1}:*` thereafter.

Load-bearing details:
- **`dryRun` defaults to on.** The fetch loop still runs and `fetchedCount` still increments,
  but nothing is written and `lastSyncedUid` is not advanced — only the status is reset to
  `IDLE`. `storedCount: 0` with a non-zero `fetchedCount` almost always means a dry run.
- **The watermark only advances on stored messages.** `lastUid` is updated inside the
  `if (!dryRun && msg.source)` branch, so a message with no source never moves it.
- On any throw the `SyncState` is set to `ERROR` (best-effort) and the error re-raised; the
  `finally` block always releases the mailbox lock, drops the connection from
  `activeConnections`, and logs out.
- `syncAll()` iterates active accounts sequentially and collects per-account failures into an
  `errors[]` array rather than aborting — one dead mailbox does not block the rest.

`ImapIngestionService.ingestAccount` (`POST /email-sync/:id/ingest`) is a **parallel path
that writes `EmailMessage` rows no downstream stage reads.** It is not part of this pipeline.

## Stage 2 — Parse

[`parseRawEmail()`](mex://method:940ed16e36f19dc57addfa6a20d46be5) runs `mailparser`'s
`simpleParser` over `RawEmail.rawSource` and upserts a `ParsedEmail` keyed on `rawEmailId`,
with `update: {}` — re-parsing an already-parsed email is a deliberate no-op. It records
`hasUnsubscribe` from the presence of the `list-unsubscribe` header, which is the single
input that later marks an email as a newsletter.

## Stage 3 — Normalize

[`normalizeEmail()`](mex://method:29d499ec20a1a63a78f8978b7722144c) does two jobs at once:

1. **Content cleanup** via `EmailNormalizer.normalize` — strip HTML, decode entities, remove
   quoted replies and signatures, collapse whitespace, and extract links (including an
   `unsubscribeLink`, detected from both URL shape and anchor text).
2. **Rule-based pre-classification** via
   [`RulesEngineService.classify()`](mex://method:f875eab2a3ace27826f72eae169d9a10), which runs
   every matcher, scores the matches per category, picks the best, and returns
   `ruleCategory` / `ruleConfidence` / `ruleReasons`. With no match it returns
   `unknown` / `low`.

Unlike the other stages this upsert **does** write on conflict: `update` refreshes
`cleanedText`, links, and all three rule fields. That is what makes
`POST /normalization/reprocess` meaningful after a normalizer or rules change — it re-runs
every already-normalized email in place. It does not invalidate downstream classifications.

## Stage 4 — Classify

[`classifyEmail()`](mex://method:e10462dcc893b10a8c881fe8d9d9e6ea) returns the existing
row immediately if one exists, then checks the enabled **sender rules**
(`SenderRule`, managed at `/sender-rules`) against `parsedEmail.fromAddress` and
`senderDomain`. A match writes the row directly with no AI call: the rule's category,
`needsReview: false`, `confidence: high`, `providerUsed: "sender-rule"`, `senderRuleId`,
and `rawResponse` = `{ ruleId, matchType, pattern, matchedOn }`. Precedence is `address` >
`domain` > `domain_suffix` > `glob` > `regex`, then longer pattern, older rule, id. A rule
whose stored category fails the output schema falls through to AI. The compiled rules are
cached in `SenderRulesService` and refreshed only by writes through `/sender-rules` (restart
after direct DB edits); a batch uses one snapshot. Only without a usable match does it
branch on the **active provider type**:

- **LLM path** (any provider but `typesafe`): builds a prompt from the normalized email *plus
  the rules-engine verdict as a hint*, and calls `AiProviderService.complete` with
  `maxTokens: Number(process.env.AI_MAX_TOKENS) || 4000`.
- **TypeSafe path** (`typesafe`): `classification.questions.ts` builds structured state
  (`email`, `signals`, `ruleEngine`; every free-text field capped — body 12,000 chars, subject
  500, from 320, domain 255, ≤10 rule reasons of ≤200 — with surrogate-safe truncation) and five
  typed questions — `category` and `recommendedAction` (choices over exactly the shared enums),
  `importance` and `urgency` (5-level scores), `sensitive` (noul) — sent in one
  `AiProviderService.judgeWith` call. `classification.judgments.ts` `mapJudgmentsToOutput` maps
  answers deterministically inside the breaker guard: levels are the 2-decimal score rounded and
  clamped; confidence is the band of the category confidence only (≥0.75 high, ≥0.5 medium,
  else low); `needsReview` fires on `unknown`, low confidence, P(sensitive) ≥ 0.5, or a
  `high`-confidence rule category that disagrees, except for pairs in `RULE_COMPATIBLE_CATEGORIES`
  (`newsletter` ↔ `marketing` / `notification` / `social`). The row is stored with `providerUsed: "typesafe"` and
  `rawResponse` = `{ questionSetVersion, reviewPolicyVersion, model, raw }` (the exact response
  body plus both version constants).

The failure split is deliberate and load-bearing:
- Provider, breaker, or rate-limit failure → **the error propagates**, no row is written, the
  email stays in the `classification: null` set and is retried next run.
- A response that arrived but does not parse or does not satisfy
  `EmailClassificationOutputSchema` → the `unknown` / `needsReview: true` fallback row is
  written with `providerUsed: "fallback"` and the message stored in `classificationError`.
  This is **LLM path only**. The TypeSafe path never writes a fallback row (fallback rows are
  never retried). A non-JSON 2xx (`InvalidProviderResponseError`, kind `unparseable`) is systemic:
  a breaker failure (short hold) that propagates like any provider error and stops the batch.
- Per-email TypeSafe failures — a 422 (`ProviderRequestRejectedError`) or JSON that fails
  `TypeSafeResponseSchema` / answers that cannot be mapped (`InvalidProviderResponseError`, kind
  `invalid_shape`): no row, counted under `errors` by `processUnclassified`, which continues with
  the next email but stops the batch (rest counted as `skipped`) after
  `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_REJECTIONS` (3) such failures in a row, mixed. These do not open the breaker,
  so a systemic case shows up only in that error log and the run's `errors` count.

[`processUnclassified()`](mex://method:82aa62e49f39025ac1dff75ffd88c693) first runs the
**sender-rule pass over every candidate** (rules compiled once per run), **before the
breaker check**, so rule-matched mail is classified even while the breaker is open; the
result's `ruleClassified` counts those (they are included in `processed`). Only the
non-matching emails go on. It then checks the
breaker **before the AI loop** and returns them all as `skipped` if it is open, and
breaks out of the loop on a `BreakerOpenError` mid-batch rather than logging one failure per
remaining email. A run that reports a large `skipped` is a breaker event (or, on TypeSafe, a run of
per-email failures), not a bug. Emails are processed newest first (`rawEmail.internalDate` desc,
then id desc), so repeatedly failing emails sink to the tail and cannot starve new mail.

`POST /classification/run` defaults to **today's mail only** (`cutoff` = local midnight,
compared against `rawEmail.internalDate`). Use `?since=YYYY-MM-DD` for a wider window or
`?all=true` for a full backfill. This is why `scripts/daily-digest.sh` passes
`?since=<yesterday>` — the default cutoff would drop overnight mail.

## Adding or changing a stage

Follow the batch shape in `context/conventions.md`: a single-record method plus a driver that
queries the null relation, loops, counts, and never lets one bad record abort the batch. A new
stage also needs its module in `AppModule` and, if it is to run on schedule, a `curl` line in
`scripts/daily-digest.sh` — nothing chains stages automatically.
